title: London's Diwali on the Square Returns October 25 With 200 Dancers
excerpt: Trafalgar Square hosts a free Festival of Lights on Sunday, October 25, 2026, from 1pm to 7pm, with Leicester's Diwali Day following on November 8.
body:
• Diwali on the Square returns to Trafalgar Square on Sunday, October 25, 2026, from 1pm to 7pm, and entry is free with no ticket required.
  • The programme opens with 200 dancers and continues with music and dance from London's Hindu, Sikh and Jain communities, plus a Ramayana puppet show for families.
  • Visitors can try sari and turban tying, yoga and meditation, arts and crafts and dance workshops, with vegetarian and vegan food stalls across the Square.
  • For diaspora families travelling in: use Charing Cross station, arrive early for bag searches, and check the official Mayor of London page before you travel for any late changes.

Trafalgar Square will host London's flagship Diwali celebration again this autumn. Mayor Sadiq Khan has confirmed Diwali on the Square for Sunday, October 25, from 1pm to 7pm, according to City Hall. The event is free, family-friendly and open to visitors of all backgrounds.

The afternoon is built around the main stage at the heart of the Square. It opens with a large group dance involving 200 performers, followed by music and dance showcasing the cultural heritage of London's Hindu, Sikh and Jain communities. For many diaspora families in the capital and the South East, this is the one public Diwali gathering that brings those three traditions together in a single programme.

What to expect on the day

Around the Square, organisers are planning activity zones rather than a single stage show. City Hall lists arts and crafts, storytelling, yoga and meditation, and dance workshops through the afternoon. Families can watch StoryHour UK's Ramayana Puppet Show, which retells the Diwali story with handcrafted puppets, music and narration.

Food is a central part of the plan. Stalls will serve vegetarian and vegan dishes throughout the day, and previous editions have added a market, sari and turban tying demonstrations, henna and children's activities. The volunteer-led Diwali in London committee delivers the event with City Hall. This year's committee theme focuses on youth, honouring values passed down by elders while giving young people a role in carrying them forward through service and community action.

"Light will always triumph over darkness, good will defeat evil, and compassion and goodwill can overcome division and despair."

— Sadiq Khan, Mayor of London

Khan described the celebration as a highlight of London's cultural calendar and a recognition of the contribution Hindu, Sikh and Jain Londoners make to the city. Headline partner for 2026 is Remitly, with Lidl and Jio Hotstar as associate partners, according to the Mayor of London announcement.

Beyond London: Leicester's Diwali Day

Readers planning a Diwali trip beyond London should also note Leicester, home to one of Britain's best-known Diwali celebrations. Leicester City Council says Diwali Day activities will return to Cossington Recreation Ground on Sunday, November 8, with community dance and music on stage, food vendors, arts and crafts stalls and a children's funfair.

The council says the popular Wheel of Light will return to Belgrave Road, and rangoli artworks will be on display at Belgrave Neighbourhood Centre. Leicester's Diwali lights will be switched on without a ceremony about two weeks before Diwali Day. There will be no public fireworks display in Leicester this year, a decision the council links to crowd safety and congestion concerns raised by the local Safety Advisory Group. Full details are on the Leicester City Council page.

Practical tips for diaspora visitors

For Trafalgar Square, the nearest station is Charing Cross, with Leicester Square, Embankment, Covent Garden and Piccadilly Circus also within walking distance. Expect bag searches at entrances and road closures around the Square, so public transport is the practical choice. No ticket is needed, but arriving before the 1pm opening dance gives families the best chance to see the full opening sequence and find space near the activity zones.

If you are visiting London for the weekend, combine the Square with Leicester only if you plan the rail journey separately — the two headline dates are two weeks apart, on October 25 and November 8. Check both official pages again in the week before you travel, as organisers may update timings, access routes and stall line-ups.

Why it matters

Diwali, the Festival of Lights, marks the victory of light over darkness and knowledge over ignorance for Hindus, Sikhs and Jains. In London, the Square celebration has become a civic moment as well as a religious one — a place where second- and third-generation families can celebrate publicly, and where neighbours who do not celebrate at home can learn the story, taste the food and join the workshops. That open, city-centre format is what keeps drawing tens of thousands back each year.
